_README: Template only. Copy to ~/.config/blkchain/mcp-clients.json (mode 0600, directory 0700) or to the path named by BLKCHAIN_MCP_CLIENT_CONFIG, and replace the placeholder paths. This entry drives Burp Suite Pro through its MCP server, reached over the stdio proxy jar Burp ships; --sse-url is Burp's own MCP listener. host=local is required: a stdio server without it runs inside the chat sandbox container, which has no network and could never reach Burp on loopback. A local command must be an absolute path. allow_tools holds every tool this Burp MCP server advertises, so the agent has full functionality; registration fails if a listed tool is absent, so trim the list to match your Burp version. Seven of them are hazardous and are listed deliberately. send_http1_request and send_http2_request carry the largest consequence: they send requests out through Burp and reach no code-side gate at all. They do not pass the engagement web scope check, the RoE, or Safe-mode approval, so this allow_tools list is the only authorization boundary for them, and an operator who leaves them in has granted a chat turn the ability to reach any host Burp can reach. The injection chain is direct: get_proxy_http_history_regex and get_proxy_websocket_history_regex return target-controlled bytes into the same turn that can call those two send tools. The remaining five: output_project_options and output_user_options dump configuration that can carry credentials into model context, set_project_options and set_user_options rewrite that configuration, and set_task_execution_engine_state pauses or resumes the scanner. Remove all seven for a read-mostly setup. MCP tool results are untrusted data. This file configures blk's outbound MCP clients and is separate from the blk mcp server.
